question: can the frozen corpora be re-derived from the pinned Mathlib, or is the freeze only a record?
mathlib: 2ec0166b31100827cd34bacca4d3b9ea3da9d618, present on the host at the pinned commit

result.D4: content leak FIXED, ordering FIXED, end-to-end rerun still owed
result.D7: FIXED and verified without a rerun

defects_found_and_fixed.id: file-hash freeze is unverifiable by construction
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: every record carries a wall-clock provenance.at, so the file sha256 differs on every run and always will, even when the data is byte-identical in content. The sealed GENERATION_RECEIPT hashes only the file.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: write_jsonl now also seals content_digest, a sha256 over the ordered content_hash list
defects_found_and_fixed.note: adding this immediately exposed the two defects below. A freeze nobody can check hides whatever it is hiding.

defects_found_and_fixed.id: D4 leaked the mkdtemp path into the hashed body
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: lean prints the absolute path of the file it is given, and that text was stored in the record's error field, which content_hash covers. Every one of the 800 records therefore changed hash on every run.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the temp path is rewritten to a stable placeholder before the error is recorded
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: grep for /var/folders/ in the regenerated D4 returns 0

defects_found_and_fixed.id: D4 record order followed Lean worker completion
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: D4 is the only source built by a worker pool, so records arrive in whatever order six parallel lean processes finish. content_digest is order-sensitive by design, so the ordering alone made D4 unfreezable. Measured: the first record was a different theorem between two runs.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: not yet end to end; the content fix is verified and the sort is deterministic by construction, but a second full run under the fixed code is still owed. That run is about an hour of Lean.

defects_found_and_fixed.id: D7 ids came from the salted builtin hash
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: ids were built with hash(tac) & 0xFFFF, and str.__hash__ is salted per interpreter unless PYTHONHASHSEED is pinned. 30 of 86 ids moved between two runs over identical inputs.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: all 30 affected suffixes recompute exactly from _stable_tag applied to a record field. Verified by recomputation, so no rerun was needed.

method_note: my first comparison used the pre-fix corpus as the baseline, which makes a difference the expected outcome rather than a failure. The correct baseline is fixed-code against fixed-code. D7 could be settled by recomputing the ids directly; D4's ordering cannot, and is recorded as owed rather than claimed.
why_this_matters: D4 is the training corpus for the repair controller, and its records are real Lean compiler errors. A repair corpus that cannot be regenerated is one whose contamination boundary and split assignment cannot be re-checked either.
